title: The infinitesimal lift sheaf for algebraic spaces is a quasi-coherent pseudo-torsor
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]; local finite presentation is tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a first order thickening of schemes over $S$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with square-zero quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$, and let $a_0:T_0\to X$ and $b:T\to Y$ satisfy $fa_0=bj$. No affineness assumption is made. Write $\Omega_{X/Y}$ for the relative differential module on the small etale ringed site of $X$, representing derivations of $\mathcal O_X$ which vanish on the image of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$; on compatible etale scheme charts its pullback is the usual scheme relative differential module [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. For a map of ringed sites $g$, module pullback means $g^*M=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{source}}\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathrm{target}}}g^{-1}M$. Put $E=a_0^*\Omega_{X/Y}$ on $(T_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$, and regard $\mathcal I$ as an $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-module via the quotient map, since $\mathcal I^2=0$. Let $H$ be the Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-module obtained by restricting $j_*\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(E,\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}})$ to Zariski opens, where $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the etale sheaf on $(T_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$ associated to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-module $\mathcal I$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], internal Hom means the sheaf of homomorphisms of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on each localized etale site, and $j_*$ is direct image along the thickening. Then $H$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the rule
$$\mathcal L(u:U\to T)=\{a:U\to X\text{ over }S\mid fa=bu,\ a|_{U_0}=a_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}\},\qquad U_0=T_0\times_TU,$$
with restriction by composition, is a sheaf of sets; fibre products here are sheaf fibre products, agreeing with scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. The associated abelian etale sheaf $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] acts on $\mathcal L$, naturally under restriction. For every $u:U\to T$ and every $a\in\mathcal L(U)$, the map $h\mapsto h\cdot a$ is a bijection $H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)\to\mathcal L(U)$. Under the relative derivation interpretation of $H_{\mathrm{et}}$, the action adds the derivation to the ring-sheaf map of a lift. No local or global existence of a lift is asserted.

source.place: Tags 061A (lemma-sheaf), 061C (lemma-action-sheaf), 061D (remark-special-case); finite presentation of relative differentials: Tag 05ZF (lemma-finite-presentation-differentials); quasi-coherence of internal Hom: Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), (6). The final paragraph of Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth) uses these facts on an affine test; the present statement only identifies the pseudo-torsor and does not assert nonemptiness.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-relative-differentials-finite-presentation], $\Omega_{X/Y}$ has local finite presentations. Tensor pullback is a left adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], hence preserves their cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Pulling back a finite free presentation gives a finite free presentation of $E=a_0^*\Omega_{X/Y}$ on a covering of $(T_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$; pullback sends each basis vector to the corresponding basis vector. Thus $E$ is of finite presentation and quasi-coherent on this site. The ideal $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-module: on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with ideal $J$, it is the module $J$ over $A/J$, since $J^2=0$. These local descriptions agree on restriction.

source.place: Tag 05ZF; tensor pullback of finite free presentations

proof.text: Put $K=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(E,\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}})$. On an etale chart where $\mathcal O^{m}\xrightarrow{A}\mathcal O^{n}\to E\to0$ is a finite presentation, $K$ is the kernel of $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}}^{n}\xrightarrow{A^t}\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}}^{m}$: a homomorphism is a tuple of images of the $n$ generators, and factors through $E$ exactly when each of the $m$ relations vanishes. This identification commutes with restriction because it sends a homomorphism to its generator images. Here $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}}$ is quasi-coherent on $(T_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$, being the image of the quasi-coherent Zariski module $\mathcal I$ of step 1 under the equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Finite sums and kernels are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]; quasi-coherence is local by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Therefore $K$ is quasi-coherent. The closed immersion result [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules] implies that $j_*K$ is quasi-coherent on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], its restriction $H$ to Zariski opens is quasi-coherent, and the counit gives a canonical isomorphism $H_{\mathrm{et}}\cong j_*K$. This is the translation sheaf specified in the statement.

For an etale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$, compatible lifts $a_i$ glue uniquely to $a:U\to X$: algebraic spaces are fppf sheaves by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and this covering is an fpqc covering by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], so [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] applies. The maps $fa$ and $bu$ agree on the covering and hence agree globally by the same statement for $Y$. The base-changed covering of $U_0$ similarly checks $a|_{U_0}=a_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}$. Uniqueness holds because it holds for maps into $X$. Restrictions are composition, so $\mathcal L$ is a sheaf.

Fix $u:U\to T$ and a lift $a\in\mathcal L(U)$. The base change $U_0\hookrightarrow U$ is square-zero with ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_U$: locally it is the quotient $B\to B/JB$ with $(JB)^2=0$. Since $u$ is etale, hence flat [def-weil-etale-morphism], $u^*\mathcal I=\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal I\mathcal O_U$ is an isomorphism (locally $J\otimes_AB\cong JB$), so the etale module of this ideal on $(U_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the restriction of $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{et}}$. Use [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] for maps into $X$ over $S$, and its naturality for $f:X\to Y$. It identifies maps $c:U\to X$ restricting to $a_0|_{U_0}$ with $S$-derivations $D=c^\sharp-a^\sharp$ into this ideal. The equation $fc=bu=fa$ is equivalent to $D\circ f^\sharp=0$, since the difference coordinate for $fa$ is zero precisely at $fa$. By the defining universal property of $\Omega_{X/Y}$ and the tensor adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], these relative derivations are exactly $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{U_0}}(a_0|_{U_0}^*\Omega_{X/Y},\mathcal I\mathcal O_U)$. This is $(j_*K)(U)$: restriction to the localized etale site is etale pullback [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the tensor formula for pullback identifies the restricted $E$ and ideal with these modules. Step 2 therefore identifies it with $H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)$.

For $h\in H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)$ corresponding to $D$, define $h\cdot a$ by replacing $a^\sharp$ with $a^\sharp+D$, using the inverse in step 4. This is a lift over $Y$, since $D\circ f^\sharp=0$. Zero fixes $a$, and adding $D_1$ then $D_2$ gives $a^\sharp+D_1+D_2$; uniqueness in the linearization makes this an abelian group action. Its orbit map at $a$ is the inverse of the bijection of step 4, hence bijective. Restricting any ring-sheaf map or derivation restricts its sum and difference, so the same uniqueness gives $(h\cdot a)|_V=h|_V\cdot a|_V$ for every morphism $V\to U$ in $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. On an object with no lift the action is the unique map to the empty set. Thus these operations define a sheaf action everywhere without asserting existence of a lift.
